title: A fast hex dumper
description:
Print a block of memory as a hex dump, using string instructions to prepare each line.

```
00000000  48 65 6c 6c 6f 2c 20 61  73 73 65 6d 62 6c 79 21  |Hello, assembly!|
00000010  00 01 02 03                                       |....|
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .data
data:   db      "Hello, assembly!", 0, 1, 2, 3
data_len equ    $ - data
hex:    db      "0123456789abcdef"

        section .text
_start:
        mov     edi, data_len
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline
        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: The high half of a byte is `al >> 4` and the low half `al & 15`; each indexes the `hex` table (lesson 8.01).
Build one 78-byte line at a time with `rep stosb` to clear it, then fill the parts in.
requirements: Each line is built in a buffer first (filled with spaces by `rep stosb`), then written with one `write` system call.
Hex digits from a 16-byte table (`"0123456789abcdef"`) indexed by each half of a byte.
Printable bytes (32 to 126) shown as themselves, others as `.`.
stretch: Read the data to dump from a file named on the command line (lesson 8.05).
